facts.raw_span: two weeks of fever
generalized weakness, vague abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, body aches, and moderate nasal bleeding
a 2×1 cm submandibular lymph node
hepatomegaly (7 cm below the costal margin)
urea 18.8 mmol/L
creatinine 141 µmol/L
ferritin >40 000 µg/L
pancytopenia: hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL, WBC 1.7×10^3/µL, ANC 0.9×10^3/µL, platelets 2×10^3/µL
bilateral subdural hemorrhages without midline shift
bilateral pleural effusion, extensive pulmonary consolidation, thrombosis of the celiac artery with splenic infarction, mild hepatomegaly, and massive splenomegaly with infarction
13% abnormal blastoid cells of medium size with fine nuclear chromatin, unevenly distributed coarse basophilic granules, and occasional bilobed nuclei
bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular with 26% immature metachromatic blasts

concepts.why: The patient's pancytopenia, abnormal blastoid cells, and hypercellular bone marrow aspirate with immature metachromatic blasts are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia.
The patient's bilateral subdural hemorrhages, thrombosis of the celiac artery, and splenic infarction are consistent with disseminated intravascular coagulation.
The patient's elevated ferritin level, pancytopenia, and histiocytes demonstrating erythrophagocytosis are consistent with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
The patient's fever, generalized weakness, and extensive pulmonary consolidation are consistent with sepsis.
The patient's thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and thrombosis of the celiac artery are consistent with thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.
The patient's hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and multi-organ involvement are consistent with multi-organ failure.
The patient's pancytopenia, abnormal blastoid cells, and hypercellular bone marrow aspirate with immature metachromatic blasts are consistent with myelodysplastic syndrome.
The patient's fever, generalized weakness, and hemorrhagic manifestations are consistent with hemorrhagic fever.

rationales.F07: Elevated ferritin levels are characteristic of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
rationales.F08: Pancytopenia is a common feature of bone marrow failure syndromes, including acute myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndrome.
rationales.F11: The presence of abnormal blastoid cells in the peripheral smear is highly suggestive of acute myeloid leukemia.
rationales.F12: The bone marrow aspirate showing immature metachromatic blasts is diagnostic of acute myeloid leukemia.
